rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty builder trees go (ficus, eucalyptus, jacarandas, magnolias, mostly in a row along the back fences; four queen palms 3 m from the house fronts); six come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the grill, the swing set, the adirondack chair and on the open lot corners.

trees.why: the back yard with the kettle grill (1.3 m off): a jacaranda over the cook
the yard with the swing set, 2.6 m from it: shade over the children's swings
the west back yards, 45 m on along the back fence line: the one tree of that stretch
the east back yard of the southern row, 6 m from the house: the yard's tree
the west corner lot by the adirondack chair: shade for whoever sits there
the open lot corner at the south, 24 m from any wall: a full jacaranda where there is room for it
